claim: Incorporating Vitamin D3 into nanostructured lipid carriers (NLC) significantly enhances intestinal absorption compared to conventional oil solutions.
scope_conditions: In vivo rat model, oral gavage 2500 IU, Precirol-based NLC vs Miglyol oil solution
quoted_support: The vitamin D3 Intestinal absorption enhanced by the incorporating in NLCs... The NLC formulation presented the faster appearance of vitamin D3 in the plasma than the oily solution formulation. Furthermore, the NLC formulation resulted in more prolonged vitamin D3 plasma level.

claim: NLC particles in nano-size ranges cross intestinal permeability barriers via Peyer's patches and M-cells, enabling lymphatic transport that bypasses liver first-pass metabolism.
stance_target: mechanism of enhanced bioavailability from lipid nanoparticles
quoted_support: Nano-particle transposition is mediated by Peyer's patches (M cells) in the small intestine. Once these particles enter the systemic circulation through lymphatic transport, the oral drug absorption is improved. Moreover, by passing the liver through lymphatic transport first-pass metabolism is reduced and consequently oral drug bioavailability is enhanced.

claim: Vitamin D3 is fat-soluble and cannot be dispersed in aqueous media; encapsulation in lipid carriers provides aqueous dispersion while preserving potency.
stance_target: fat-soluble nature of D3 requires oil/lipid carrier for absorption
quoted_support: Hydrophobic vitamins like vitamin D3 cannot be dispersed in aqueous mediums (most of beverages) and are sensitive to oxidation, hence the fact that encapsulation might provide a proper way to preserve their potency and an appropriate aqueous dispersion to fortify beverages.
numbers: 200-400 IU suggested daily dose for adults (stated in paper)

claim: Precirol-based NLC showed superior physical stability over Compritol-based NLC; optimum Poloxamer407 concentration of 3% prevented particle agglomeration with 60-day stability.
stance_target: formulation science for stable D3 lipid carriers
scope_conditions: NLC formulation F3 tested at 25°C for 60 days
quoted_support: The Precirol-based NLC showed superiority over Compritol-based NLC in the point of physical stability. Results clearly suggested that an optimum concentration of 3% of Poloxamer407 or 2% of Tween20 was sufficient to cover the surface of nanoparticles effectively and prevent agglomeration during the homogenization process.
